learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of mathematics and other basic sciences inherent to their engineering specialty, at a level that allows acquiring the rest of the degree's competencies.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and appropriately apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that comply with established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in the field of their specialty.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers and people from other disciplines.
Uses integral calculus to solve physical and geometric problems.

teaching_methods: Development, drafting and presentation of reports, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams and/or control points
Professor's presentation in the classroom, in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects (Lectures, participatory classes)
Completion of exercises individually and in teams
Computer simulation practices, individually and/or in teams

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Technical ability, involvement in the project/PBL, work carried out, results obtained, documentation submitted, technical presentation and defense

assessment_rules: Individual written and oral tests (80%) have equivalent recovery mechanisms. Reports on exercises, case studies, and practical work (10%) are recovered through continuous assessment or a written recovery (75%) combined with a control point (25%). Technical ability, project involvement, and technical presentation (10%) contribute to the final grade; for some specific competencies, no explicit recovery mechanisms are stated, implying continuous assessment where applicable.
